what: The coverage floor `scripts/ci.sh coverage` fails under, and the per-file baseline it compares every file against. `scripts/coverage-check.py` reads both, and compares an uncovered line count per file because a line count is an integer and a slide is what this file is for; the sentences above that file's main() are the reasoning.

`floor` is moved by hand, one line at a time: raise `lines_percent` to `as_measured_percent` when a change earns it, and leave the four provenance fields naming the measurement it was set from. `--update` deliberately does not touch it.

`baseline` is measured: `python3 scripts/coverage-check.py --update --baseline .config/coverage-baseline.json --report <export.json>` rewrites it (and only it) from an llvm-cov export. A deliberate slide, a rename, a split or a file that stopped being compiled is a pull request that runs that command and says why.

`slack_lines` is the per-file room the environment needs, not a policy. Seven runs of the same suite over the same tree on 2026-10-06 said 84.2379, 84.2379, 84.2672, 84.2599, 84.2672, 84.2672 and 84.2672% of lines -- 2152 uncovered at the worst, 2148 at the best -- and three files of 29 account for all of it: `crates/whirl-cli/src/daemon/macos.rs` (91 uncovered in five runs, 95 in two), `crates/whirld/src/worker.rs` (86 or 87), `crates/whirld/src/plan.rs` (52 or 53). It is set to the widest per-file swing seen, 4 lines, plus two: it is what keeps this job from being red on a green change, and a slide is wider than it.

The floor sits under the measured number for the same reason, and the two rules are layered: 84.1 leaves 18 uncovered lines of room over the 2152 measured, above the per-file slack (6), so a slide inside one file past its slack trips the per-file rule while the total still holds, and a slide spread thin across the workspace trips the floor while no file does. A few lines spread over several files are under both and are not caught; that is the size of the hole.
